observation: The hero is a mosaic. A large 752x732 featured card with a full-bleed cartoon image sits on the left, and two stacked cards sit on the right, each with an image on top and text below. The featured card puts its title over the image on a dark gradient.
evidence: Image rects: 752x732 at x146,y218; two 374x210 images at x919. The hero title is white bold sans over a gradient. facts report 8 gradient backgrounds.

evidence: Natural size [720,380] against a rendered rect of 752x732.

observation: Category labels are small red filled uppercase tags with white bold, letter-spaced text and square corners. They appear on every card and on the hero.
evidence: Red rgb(180,54,31) is the background on 33 elements. Labels read SCIENCE, EDUCATION, ONLINE EDUCATION and GENERAL.

observation: The palette is a warm off-white page background with white cards, navy bars and a single brick-red accent. Body text is near-black navy, and metadata is grey-blue.
evidence: body_bg rgb(246,244,239); card backgrounds rgb(255,255,255) on 42 elements; navy rgb(20,33,61); accent rgb(180,54,31); text rgb(27,31,42), with rgb(102,112,133) on 133 elements.

observation: Two font families are paired. A system-ui sans (rendered like Inter or Helvetica) is used for headings, labels and UI. Georgia serif is used for excerpts, the tagline, the site title and the search placeholder.
evidence: fonts_by_element_count: system-ui 384, Georgia 202. Slice 1 shows excerpts in grey serif.

observation: Each section heading is an uppercase bold sans h2 with a thick dark underline running across the column. A red 'View all →' link is right-aligned on the same row.
evidence: h2 is 32px/700 in the facts, though the section headings appear smaller. Slices 0-3 show headings such as SCIENCE, COLLEGE AND UNIVERSITY and EDUCATIONS, each followed by 'View all →'.

observation: The content is split into sections by category. Each has a 3-column grid of cards that wraps, so the last row often holds 2 cards and leaves an empty third column.
evidence: 7 section elements and 30 article elements; 17 grid containers. Cards sit at x=147, 424 and 702 with width about 255. Slices 1-3 show empty third slots.

observation: The page uses a two-column layout: a main column about 812px wide (x146-958) and a sidebar about 300px wide (x994-1294) containing Author Info, Popular, Latest Posts, Category, Tags and Search. The sidebar ends well before the main column does.
evidence: Slice 0 shows the AUTHOR INFO heading at x994. The aside count is 1. In slice 2 the sidebar ends at the Search box while main content continues.

observation: Cards are white rectangles with a thin light border and a small corner radius. No box shadows are used. Each card stacks a 255x144 image, a red tag, a bold sans title, a 'By WebEditor · date' meta line and, in some sections, a serif excerpt.
evidence: box_shadows 0; border_radius_buckets: 72 elements at 1-7px, 503 at 0. Image rects are 255x144.

observation: Card heights vary with title length. In some rows shorter cards leave empty white space at the bottom, and content is top-aligned.
evidence: Slice 1, 'How to prepare for JEE Advanced 2020?' has a blank lower half, and the sibling cards in that row stretch to the same height.

observation: Only the Science cards carry excerpts, set in grey Georgia and ending with an ellipsis. The cards in other sections show title and meta only.
evidence: Slice 1 shows excerpts like 'US President Donald Trump made an announcement...' in the Science row and in the first College card. Other rows have none.

observation: Several cards have no photo. They use a navy diagonal-gradient placeholder with the category name in white uppercase letter-spaced text centred on it.

observation: The page is flat in styling. There are no shadows, backdrop blur, animations or transforms. It has 32 transitions, and the only gradients are the hero overlay and the placeholder panels.

observation: The DOM uses semantic landmarks and a small, hand-written class vocabulary. It has no scripts, one stylesheet, one inline style attribute and no SVGs.
